text:
Democrats criticise Nvidia after Trump's intervention sees CEO Huang resinstated
Hello and welcome to the US politics live blog.
Nvidia’s decision to reinstate Jensen Huang as CEO sends a message “that the national security of this country is not as important as your relationship with president Trump,” Democratic senator Ruben Gallego said.
Huang, who co-founded the company in 1993, was ousted by the board after allegations that he had three affairs, including one with a suspected Chinese spy and two with employees. But the Nvidia board reinstated him after an intervention from the US president.
“We also have to figure out how corporate America doesn’t take a bad lesson from this, and thinks that somehow it’s OK for them to evade national security for the purposes of just selling more,” Gallego, an Arizona Democrat considering a White House campaign, said.
Meanwhile, California representative Ro Khanna wrote on social media that “rules should apply to everyone,” noting that “the rich + powerful, like Jensen, do not get to evade export controls or accountability just because it props up the stock price.”
Huang returned to the company’s HQ in Santa Clara, California, on Monday and received a hero’s welcome, with crowds of employees chanting “Jensen, Jensen, Jensen!”
President Trump made up to $15m on his holdings of Nvidia stock after the US chipmaker’s share price soared on the surprise return of Huang.
His return as CEO came despite Huang being subject to several government and internal investigations, shareholder lawsuits and accusations that he’s a national security threat.
Nvidia is one of the most valuable businesses in the world, worth about $4tn, and the entire AI ecosphere relies on it. The company engineers advanced chips used to train AI models and power tech firms such as OpenAI, Anthropic and Google.
In other developments:
- US smbassador to Israel Mike Huckabee has cast doubt on whether Washington would end its $3.8bn in annual military aid to Israel by the end of this year, as promised by Trump on the day of this month’s midterm elections. In his surprise announcement as voters headed to the polls on 3 November, Trump said he had made a deal with prime minister Benjamin Netanyahu several months earlier to stop providing Israel with around $4bn in annual US funding.
- Speaking at the US Department of Justice, Trump railed against the commutations of death row inmates’ sentences by California’s governor, Gavin Newsom. Newsom responded by criticizing Trump for “selling” pardons and for demanding the execution of five wrongfully convicted young New Yorkers of color in 1989.
- Jimmy Gomez will resign from Congress after a House ethics report released on Monday found “substantial evidence” that the California Democrat had “engaged in sexual misconduct”, including by “making unwelcome sexual advances and sexual contact toward a House staffer”. The 19-page report from the House ethics committee found that Gomez “made unwanted sexual advances” toward a House staffer on two occasions, “including an incident in which he made sexual contact with her and another in which he was ‘forceful’ with her in his congressional office”.
digest_he:
החלטת דירקטוריון Nvidia להחזיר את ג'נסן הואנג לתפקיד המנכ״ל לאחר התערבות של הנשיא טראמפ עוררה ביקורת חריפה מצד מחוקקים דמוקרטים בארצות הברית. הואנג הודח בעבר בעקבות טענות להתנהלות בלתי הולמת, אך חזר לתפקידו לקול תשואות העובדים. פוליטיקאים דמוקרטים, ובהם הסנטור כריס ואן הולן ורוב ג'אגו, טענו כי המהלך משקף שחיתות פוליטית ומעביר מסר שלילי לחברות הענק בארצות הברית בכל הנוגע לציתות לכללי ייצוא וביטחון לאומי. במקביל, הנשיא טראמפ רשם רווח משמעותי מהחזקותיו במניות החברה בעקבות הזינוק בשער המניה עם חזרתו של הואנג.

בדיווחים נוספים מתוך אירועי השעה בארצות הברית, השגריר האמריקאי בישראל מייק האקבי הביע ספק לגבי האפשרות שוושינגטון תסיים את סיוע החוץ הצבאי לישראל עד סוף השנה הנוכחית, בהתאם להצהרה קודמת של טראמפ. כמו כן, חבר הקונגרס ג'ימי גומז הודיע על התפטרותו בעקבות דו
